stops.note: the Boston Morning Post printed 'o.k.' on 23 March 1839 as a joke abbreviation of 'oll korrect', part of a fad for misspelled initials, as the linguist Allen Walker Read showed in the 1960s
Martin Van Buren's re-election campaign adopted it for his nickname 'Old Kinderhook', spreading it nationwide through 'O.K. Clubs'
spelled out as a word; now among the most widely recognised expressions in the world's languages

current_meaning: satisfactory; all right; used to express agreement
